To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we proposed and analyzed a perturbed inertia primal dual dynamical system for linearly constrained convex problems, and proved its fast convergence properties, which are the extensions of the existing results on the perturbed inertial dynamical system for the unconstrained case.

we propose a perturbed primal dual dynamic with inertial terms both in primal and dual variables and with damping and scaling terms, and we prove its asymptotic properties and fast convergence properties.

we proposed a perturbed inertially primal dual dynamic with scaling and damping coefficients, for a linear constrained convex optimization problem, and discussed the asymptotic convergence properties of the dynamic by a Lyapounov approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) the inertial primal dual dynamics with scaling coefficients, (2) the inertial dynamics with damping coefficients, (3) the perturbed inertial dynamics with scaling coefficients and damping coefficients, (4) the perturbed primal dual dynamics.

the following aspects: (a) the perturbed primal dual dynamics, (b) the inertial terms both in the primal and dual variables of the dynamic, (c) the damping and time scaling coefficient in the dynamic, (d) the Lyapunov function and its properties, (e) the fast convergence of the dynamic.

the following topics: (a) the perturbed inertial dynamical system for a convex optimization problem; (b) the perturbed primal dual dynamical system with damping and scaling coefficient for the linearly constrained optimization problem; (c) the asymptotic properties and the fast convergence properties of the proposed dynamical systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the proposed perturbed inertial dynamic with damping and time scale coefficients is more general than the existing inertial dynamical models for linearly constrained convex minimization problem.
, the proposed dynamic can be used to solve the linearly constrained optimization problem in Hilbert spaces, which has a better convergence property than the existing ones.

the perturbed inertial dynamic with damping and time-scaling coefficients for linearly constrained convex minimization problem is a powerful tool for solving the linearly constrained optimization problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inertial terms in the proposed dynamic can be viewed as a tool to improve the convergence rate of the primal dual dynamics for linearly constrained convex minimization problems.

the proposed perturbed inertial dual dynamics is the first one for the linearly constrained problem with fast convergence properties, and that the proposed perturbation technique for the primal dynamics can also be used for the primal dual dynamics for the unconstrained problem.

the proposed dynamic has the following properties: (1) the dynamic has a fast asymptotic convergence rate; (2) the dynamic has an asymptotic convergence rate independent of the initial point; (3) the dynamic has no need of the Lipschitz continuous gradient assumption on the objective function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scaling and damping parameters can be chosen freely to obtain the best performance.
, with the help of scaling coefficients, we can achieve the same asymptotic properties as those of the inertial primal dual dynamical systems with damping coefficients.
, by using a suitable scaling coefficient, one can obtain a dynamic with a fast convergence rate.
